artifacts.summary: Implementation summary covering all 4 phases: git ls-files enumeration replacement, header comment update, positive-detection fixture verification, and deploy propagation.

completion_data.completion_summary: Replaced find-based enumeration in check_undeclared_scripts() with git ls-files, re-derived the REPO_ROOT-relative prefix-strip and existence guard, updated the header comment, empirically verified via a positive-detection fixture that tracked-but-undeclared scripts are still caught (HARD gate passed), and propagated the fix through the deploy path -- the two literature __pycache__ FAILs are gone and the doc-lint gate exits 0.

memory_candidates.content: When adding a `git-commit-scoped.sh`-style targeted commit against a task directory whose auto-injected ephemeral excludes include a currently-existing gitignored subdirectory (e.g. specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/.lock/ held by an active task-lock), `git add <dir>/ :(exclude)<dir>/.lock/` fails with 'paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files' and exit 1 -- git treats an exclude pathspec that names an ignored path as an explicit mention, which it refuses, even though `git add <dir>/` alone (recursing without any exclude pathspec) silently skips the same ignored subdirectory with exit 0. Workaround: stage the task directory's specific subpaths (plans/, progress/, .return-meta.json, etc.) individually instead of the whole directory glob that triggers the auto-exclude injection.

To empirically verify a change to a doc-lint/enumeration check does not silently degrade into a no-op, use a three-property test: (1) diff the pre-change vs post-change output and confirm the delta is EXACTLY the expected removed findings, (2) confirm the finding count for a clean tree is zero (no regression), and (3) build a positive-detection fixture (e.g. `git add -N` an intentionally-noncompliant file) and confirm the check still reports it, then clean up and re-verify output matches baseline. This three-property pattern (skip untracked / no false positives / still catches violations) is reusable for any enumeration-method change (find -> git ls-files, glob -> index-driven, etc.).
